title: Enforce KMS tag validation and audit dedupe; add RBAC rate-bound shim
author: Anika Bose
release_notes: Adds KMS tag validation middleware, audit deduplication pipeline, and RBAC rate-bound enforcement. No breaking API changes. Feature gated and rolled out gradually.
commit_summary: add: kms tag validation middleware and unit tests
feat: audit dedupe service and hash index with TTL
chore: add feature flag and rollout script (ff:security.kms_tag_validation)
fix: tighten rbac rate-bound evaluation for operator-scoped roles
test: e2e scenario for cross-region write with invalid kms-tag rejected
description:
Motivation: We observed several incidents where tenant KMS-related requests bypassed intended residency and tagging constraints because of malformed or missing KMS metadata. Additionally, audit streams contained duplicated events (retries and multi-hops) which inflate storage and complicate forensic queries. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a gateway middleware that validates KMS usage tags (origin, provider, region, tenant_id) against the canonical kms_schema and rejects requests that fail validation, 2) an audit deduplication service that computes a stable hash for incoming audit envelopes, persists an index with short TTL to collapse duplicates and emit a single canonical event for downstream consumers, and 3) an RBAC "rate-bound" shim that limits high-privilege cross-region role assignments per operator to mitigate blast radius for cross-zone operations.

Design summary: The kms_tag_validator runs early in the gateway request pipeline. It parses the KMS metadata header (x-kms-meta) and validates it against internal policy rules defined in internal/policies/kms_schema.proto. Rules include required keys, allowed region sets per tenant, and provider whitelists. Validation failures return 4xx with structured error payloads pointing to remediation links.

The audit dedupe service is a small idempotency layer in front of our audit buffer. For each incoming envelope, we compute dedupe_hash := SHA256(sorted_headers || payload_digest || kms_proof). The hash is written into a dedupe index table with insertion_ts and ttl (default 2 hours). If a duplicate is detected, the service increments a duplicate counter and drops subsequent writes to the long-term store; a canonical entry is bubbled to downstream subscriptions. The dedupe index is sharded by tenant to avoid cross-tenant collisions.

The RBAC rate-bound shim extends the RBAC v2 evaluator. It adds a configurable per-principal windowed allowance for sensitive operations (e.g., role-grant across regions, kms-provider-switch). The default policy is conservative: max 3 cross-region grants per operator per 24h. The window and thresholds are tenant-configurable via the existing policy manager.

Compatibility & rollout: All changes are behind the feature flag security.kms_tag_validation and a traffic-splitting flag for audit.dedupe. Default flags are OFF. We will enable in the following sequence: 1) enable validator in attr-check mode (log-only) for 48h -> 2) enable hard-reject for a small canary org list -> 3) expand to 20% of traffic -> 4) full enable for hosted tier. RBAC rate-bound is on-by-default for internal operators and rolled out to customers by policy push.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests, integration tests, and an e2e that simulates retried audit envelopes and malformed kms headers. CI initially failed due to a flaky test (tests/e2e/kms-tag-validation.test.js) where the test harness timed out on the first run; we increased the harness timeout and re-ran pipelines. Final CI: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e, security-scan). See ci/pipelines/security.yml for the security gating steps.

Security review notes: The validator rejects malformed kms metadata which prevents downstream KMS allocators from making unsafe assumptions. We ensured the validator does not leak any secret material in error messages. Audit dedupe keeps only hash and minimal index info in the dedupe table; raw audit payloads continue to be stored (when canonical) and are accessible under existing retention policies. We added an optional KMS-origin proof field that can be used to correlate wrapped-key IDs without revealing plaintext key material.

Migration: Database migration scripts to add dedupe_index table are included as services/audit/dedupe/dedupe_index_schema.sql and are compatible with online deploys. Terraform updates provide IAM bindings needed for the dedupe worker under deploy/helm/values-security.yaml and terraform/modules/kms/main.tf.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Jordan Kim (reviewer): "Can we guarantee that the dedupe hash won't collide across tenants? Sharding helps but callout the salt decision."
  - Author (Anika): "We explicitly prefix the hash with tenant_id and include shard id; added comment and unit test to assert isolation. See commit 'fix: include tenant prefix in dedupe hash'"
- Marcus Feldman: "The RBAC rate-bound default seems strict for some large platform teams. Can we make it configurable per-Tenant (tenant policy override)?"
  - Author: "Yes — policy manager override added; updated docs and feature flag description. We ship with a conservative default and document how to opt-up via policy push."
- Priya Nair: "Please ensure errors from the gateway validator include remediation links and do not contain KMS ARNs or secrets."
  - Author: "Removed ARN echoing and added remediation links to error schema. Added an integration test to assert no ARN present in error messages."
- Marcus: "Approve after minor docs nit"
- Jordan: "Approve"

Merge and post-merge: After approvals we squashed and merged. Post-merge tasks: monitor metrics 'security.kms_validator.reject_rate' and 'audit.dedupe.duplicate_rate' for the first 72h. An automatic rollback playbook is included in scripts/rollout/kms-tag-gate-rollout.sh.

Related: ENG-7823 (policy schema), SEC-412 (audit hardening), OPS-119 (rollout automation).
notes: Audit dedupe TTL configurable via env: AUDIT_DEDUPE_TTL_SECONDS (default 7200)
RBAC rate-bound thresholds controlled by policy namespace 'rbac.ratebound.*'
